argument: Eleven apertures must read as one collective topology around a real negative centre, not as eleven decorative rings. The empty centre and broken arcs must carry the composition before the interface does.

With labels, readout, controls, caption, and prose hidden, the first view must leave the fossil, moving shards, and faceted membrane. It should read as a field of decisions made from openings, not an orbit diagram.

The visitor must hand attention between two distinct openings, not select one, wait on one, close a loop, or cross a grain. An incomplete or returned approach must remain geometry-neutral; pointer, touch, keyboard, and control paths must agree.
Only a confirmed distinct handoff may change actual remote opening, depth, twist, echo, and relay count. Cursor movement, colour, status, and prose cannot substitute for produced topology.

The approached source and observer must remain exact. The event must be readable in a third portal that the visitor did not enter, proving that attention was redistributed rather than answered locally.
The receiver must change its nested apertures and negative wedge, not merely brighten. Four different receivers and serial changes must remain visibly distinct in the settled field.
Four handoffs must compound in one orbit field. Delete must reconstruct the exact preceding geometry and release must restore the deterministic quiet register.

Generated WEBGL arc geometry, negative wedges, seeded portal registers, and remote aperture state are the medium. No screenshot, imported model, SVG fallback, texture, or stock particle library may carry the work.

little-critters is translated from situated proximity and reciprocal attention into a discrete handoff whose consequence arrives in an unvisited portal. Animals, eyes, characters, paper scene, palette, composition, code, examples, and API are refused.

v044 changes representation, composition, encounter, temporal behaviour, medium, and viewer task: body, fossil, moving shards, and resistance facets become a stable negative-aperture topology in which two sites hand attention to a third.
